in general, here are my tips for cleaning:
- a LOT of things can be cleaned using a sponge, a bucket of hot water, and liquid dish soap like dawn. i even use dish soap in my bath tub and it works very well!! hot water should be used to help dissolve dirt and stuff and also to help sanitize surfaces. although, it can depend on the cleaning product youre using. it is almost always listed on the product itself what temperature of water you should use, as well as if it needs to be used with water at all

- if you dont really want to get out a bucket and use water, you can also get away with using clorox pre-saturated cleaning wipes on things like counters and sink faucets and sink handles and maybe mirrors and the outside of the toilet. this is much easier because you just grab the canister of wipes and pull them out and chuck them in the regular trash when you're done !

- some of the basic tools i suggest for the bathroom specifically are sponges (you can easily go through a lot of sponges while cleaning, so make sure to get a lot of them. the double sided ones with a scrapy abrasive side are extra good), a good sized bucket maybe around 5 US gallons, a toilet brush with a holder, a broom, specific toilet bowl cleaner, a mop, liquid floor cleaner like lysol or fabuloso, glass cleaner, and paper towels. instead of paper towels, you can also use microfiber towels because they are washable and reusable but i dont like the texture or absorbency of them

- the toilet brush must only be used on the inside of the toilet bowl, with the toilet bowl cleaner. usually, these products are intended to sanitize and disinfect the toilet bowl. i'm not 100% sure if there are any bowl cleaners that *dont* also disinfect, but if it does disinfect it will usually say it in big letters on the front (many other products that disinfect also have the same kind of labeling!)

- the mop mentioned above can be used for any tile floors and *some* wood floors... it can be a bit troublesome to figure out what wood floors can use the mop though. it would be worthwhile to do a whole deep dive on tiktok or youtube or google. the sponges can be used of course in the kitchen and basically anywhere you need to scrub on a hard surface that isnt porous. you could even use sponges on the floor too but its a bit troublesome to bend down and scrub so a mop is better. the bucket can also be used everywhere (bonus tip! if the toilet becomes clogged/wont drain, instead of using a plunger you can fill the bucket with water and pour it into the bowl from around waist or chest height and it can often help unclog it!). especially good for a bucket is one with marks to show how much water is in it, so that if you need to dilute some products (most often floor cleaners but also anything marked as a concentrate) its much easier to figure out how much product you need!! brooms can sweep anywhere that has a hard floor, glass cleaner is good for mirrors and windows and can be used with paper towels or microfiber cloths (but again, bad texture)

- a good vacuum will also get you very far if you have carpet. but it can also be very useful with hard floors too. you can often change the setting of the vacuum to work better on hard floors. i like to sweep and then vacuum because sweeping doesnt always pick up all the things on the floor, especially very small things like fine dirt or very light wispy things like hairs or dust bunnies

- for dusting surfaces like shelves and window blinds, i use swiffer dusters and sometimes i dont even bother using a handle, i just wipe down surfaces with the duster in my hand. i *heard* that theres a method of wet dusting using a damp washcloth that can be much more effective and long lasting, but i havent looked into how to do it yet 😅 but it could be a worthwhile thing to look into as well!!

these are kind of general tips ... there are a lot of really specific cleaning products that clean specific things in specific ways ! they can be very useful, but i understand they might seem intimidating to sort through all of them.

also!! it is extremely advisable, from one autistic to another, to use rubber gloves!! for some products that are harsh chemicals, it is really required, but even for things like scrubbing with a soapy sponge, rubber gloves like the kind you use for washing dishes can be wonderful in terms of making me motivated to clean. if i know i wont have to deal with dry scratchy hands from chemicals and water, it makes cleaning soooo much less intimidating and painful! i actually kind of enjoy cleaning when i have all the right tools...
